name: Wishing Well
description: {T}: (effect not determinable from the given nodes — see "Could not derive"). Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery.
assumptions: Rendered the cond:sorcery_speed restriction using the standard modern templating "Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery," rather than an alternative phrasing (e.g., "Activate only as a sorcery") — the nodes only establish that a sorcery-speed restriction exists, not its exact printed wording.
Assumed the ability has no additional activation cost beyond tapping, since node C carries no cost:{...} flag.
Assumed the ability doesn't target anything, since neither C nor D carries a target flag — the effect applies to "this artifact" automatically.
couldNotDerive: The actual nature and magnitude of the ability's effect. D's flag is cond:delta=COIN, which per the schema's binding rules (bare = references a value that must be declared elsewhere with :=) should point to a value named "COIN" fixed on some node — but no node in this card's set declares COIN:= anything. What the artifact actually gains/becomes when tapped (a stat change, a type/color change, etc.) is genuinely unspecified by the given material.
Whether the card has any subtype, supertype, or rarity — none of these appear in the registry or nodes.
notes: Real card (forge-model/data/wishing-well.txt): '{T}: Put a coin counter on Wishing Well. When you do, you may cast target instant or sorcery card with mana value equal to the number of coin counters on Wishing Well from your graveyard without paying its mana cost. If that spell would be put into your graveyard, exile it instead. Activate only as a sorcery.' Mana cost/type line match ({3}{U} Artifact). The packet's 4 nodes (A cast, B enters, C tap cond:sorcery_speed, D modifier cond:delta=COIN) correctly cover only the first sentence — node D's cond:delta=COIN is in fact derivable and correct: PutCounter's CounterType$ COIN hits forgeTranslate.ts's `const type = fields.CounterType === 'P1P1' ? '+1/+1counter' : (fields.CounterType ?? 'counter')` (~line 1224), which folds any non-P1P1 CounterType straight into the literal, producing exactly this flag. The reconstructing agent still failed to read it (see below), but that's a secondary issue. The real DECOMPOSITION GAP is that everything downstream of the PutCounter — the entire 'When you do... exile it instead' clause, arguably the card's defining mechanic — is completely absent from edges.json's node/flow for this card, and the SubAbility chain that describes it never even produces an 'unmapped' trace a reviewer would notice, because forgeTranslate.ts fails silently at three consecutive DB kinds: (1) SVar:DBImmediateTrig (DB$ ImmediateTrigger) — 'ImmediateTrigger' is absent from the EFFECT_ROLE map and has no dedicated branch, so it falls into the generic `if (!role)` unmapped path (~line 1336-1361) instead of emitting a role:'trigger' / to:'stack' node the way other trigger-types are built (c.f. the addNode(...) at ~line 543) — the schema's own trigger role exists precisely for this 603.3b 'when you do' stack object and is simply never invoked. (2) SVar:TrigPlay (DB$ Play | TgtZone$ Graveyard | ValidTgts$ Instant.YouCtrl+cmcEQX,Sorcery.YouCtrl+cmcEQX | WithoutManaCost$ True | Optional$ True | ReplaceGraveyard$ Exile | AILogic$ ReplaySpell) — 'Play' also has no EFFECT_ROLE entry and no special-case handler anywhere in the file (zero grep hits for a 'Play' ek check), so no cast node (role:'cast', from:'gy', to:'stack', thing:'any', flags along the lines of 'target may cost:{0}') is ever created for casting the graveyard spell, and none of ValidTgts$'s qualifiers (Instant/Sorcery restriction, YouCtrl, or the numeric cmcEQX restriction) get parsed. (3) SVar:X (Count$CardCounters.COIN), which cmcEQX refers to, has no corresponding scaler-node logic anywhere in forgeTranslate.ts — there is no code path turning a Count$CardCounters.<Type> SVar into a role:'scaler' node with a qty:=<label> declaration for downstream cond:cmc=<label> binding, so even a fixed Play handler has nothing to bind X to yet. Separately, ReplaceGraveyard$ is never read anywhere in the file (zero grep hits) — a fourth missing piece, needed as a move/becomes node for the resolved spell's own resting zone, a case SCHEMA.md's own move-role description explicitly anticipates ('a resolved spell's own resting zone'). SVar:DBCleanup (DB$ Cleanup | ClearRemembered$ True) is correctly and deliberately dropped with no node and no unmapped noise (line 839, 'Forge-only bookkeeping, no synergy analogue') — that part is fine. This is a translation/decomposition gap in forgeTranslate.ts, not a schema gap: SCHEMA.md's trigger/cast/scaler/move roles can already express every one of the missing pieces, the translator just never wires ImmediateTrigger, Play, or ReplaceGraveyard$ up to them. Secondary, minor finding (agent misinterpretation, not itself a bug target): the reconstructing agent read cond:delta=COIN as an unresolved <field>=<label> binding reference per SCHEMA.md's binding-form rule ('bare = always references' a value fixed elsewhere via ':='), and concluded the tap ability's effect was entirely undeterminable rather than reading COIN as a literal counter-type label — worth a SCHEMA.md wording clarification (delta=<literal type name> vs delta=<bound value> are visually indistinguishable) even though it isn't a forgeTranslate.ts bug.
